scope: Actual Rust transient Heart resource owner with a valid tiny PNG fixture; not the native decode, provider, pixel or export boundary

native.fixture: Valid 20x20 RGBA8 PNG with CRC, uncompressed zlib/deflate and Adler32; expected RGBA supplied directly for this CPU-only gate

coverage: Encoded Resource length/SHA and actual MIME/container dimensions, plus decoded RGBA hash/shape binding
Owner/session/frame/manifest identity equality and stale/cross-owner isolation
Gaps, overlaps, missing/trailing bytes, overflow and unknown authored fact fields
Metadata, immutable provider packet and inbound WASM-copy reservation before invoking the copier
Exactly one successful binary extraction per derived image index; duplicate extraction creates no second copy and cancels only that session
Cancellation, malformed frames, metadata failure, copier failure and caught panic release reservations symmetrically
Owner/session capability exhaustion and explicit dispose/Drop symmetry
limitations: Two tests contain a serial process-global lifecycle matrix; not two complete end-to-end editor scenarios
The image header parser does not replace actual Canvas decode or prove compressed pixel validity
The 16KiB-per-possible-image metadata reservation is conservative and may reject ordinary large source images; common-size capacity still needs production acceptance
Budgets describe one Rust/WASM instance and stated provider copies, not measured whole-renderer or cross-worker memory
No installed Electron, whole MV, native raster parity, export or performance acceptance
